proposed statement: The co-op has a seasonal operation with a specific timeframe for citrus packing
key statement: Bosveld Citrus packs oranges (Valencias and navels), lemons and mandarins for its member growers, from large commercial farms to small growers with five or six hectares, through one packhouse in Letsitele; the season runs from the end of March (early mandarins) to about mid-September (last Valencias).

proposed statement: The current system lacks a reliable method for tracking bin ownership and packout data, leading to manual reconciliation and potential mix-ups
key statement: How will bins be labelled for scanning? Most bins belong to the growers, some numbered and some not; the co-op lends out about 3,000 of its own bins with numbers burnt in; Precious floated a clip-on plastic barcode tag that comes back to the weighbridge, and the consultant will look into what other packhouses do.

proposed statement: The client prefers to have a system where growers can see their deliveries and packout data on their phones within a day or two of the transaction
key statement: Growers can see their own deliveries and packout on their phones the same day or the day after.

proposed statement: The current system lacks a traceable method for bin identification, leading to potential mix-ups during the grading process
key statement: How will bins be labelled for scanning? Most bins belong to the growers, some numbered and some not; the co-op lends out about 3,000 of its own bins with numbers burnt in; Precious floated a clip-on plastic barcode tag that comes back to the weighbridge, and the consultant will look into what other packhouses do.

proposed statement: The weighbridge must keep working without the network to prevent trucks from waiting at the gate, which could cause fruit to sit in the sun for up to twenty trucks
key statement: Intake at the weighbridge must keep working without the network and catch up when the link is back; trucks can never be stopped at the gate.

proposed statement: The Optisort grader system is locked down with a password that the client does not have, and the supplier requires a password to be reset before providing any data exports
key statement: The Optisort grader's computer is locked down, its reports are PDFs and touching it would void the support contract, so getting packout data out automatically is uncertain and could slip; if it does, Marietjie keeps typing for a while.

proposed statement: The client uses a spreadsheet to calculate payments to growers, which is updated monthly after the board sets advance rates for different cultivars and sizes
key statement: The advance payment calculation stays in Sipho's spreadsheet for phase one, because the board changes the rates every season; the new system supplies the deliveries and packout as an export.

proposed statement: The payment calculation for growers will remain in Sipho's spreadsheet for phase one, and the new system will provide deliveries and packout data as an export for the spreadsheet
key statement: Do statements come from the new system (with Sipho uploading the advances each month) or stay in the spreadsheet?

proposed statement: Growers can only see their own deliveries, packouts, and statements to prevent sensitive information exposure
key statement: Each grower sees only their own deliveries, packouts and statements; growers must never see each other's payments.

proposed statement: The system must not allow growers to see the reason for delivery corrections to avoid unnecessary disputes
key statement: Should the grower see the reason a delivery was corrected, or only that it was?

proposed statement: Growers keep financial records for five years in physical boxes due to auditor requirements, with some records being eaten by mice.
key statement: Deliveries and statements are kept for five years (the auditors' rule), including for growers who leave.

proposed statement: The system must work on cheap Android phones with slow internet connections without consuming data.
key statement: Growers' pages must work on cheap Android phones over slow connections without using much data, as a web page opened from a link (savable to the home screen), not an app to download.

proposed statement: Growers should not have to download an app for the system, as previous apps were not installed by the target audience.
key statement: Growers' pages must work on cheap Android phones over slow connections without using much data, as a web page opened from a link (savable to the home screen), not an app to download.

proposed statement: Growers change their phone numbers, so the system must allow updating phone numbers through the office like bank details to prevent account takeover.
key statement: Bank details, and growers' phone numbers, are changed only by the office (bank details by Sipho with a letter from the bank), never by the grower from their phone, after an attempted fraud last year.

proposed statement: The system must support multiple languages including English, Afrikaans, Xitsonga, and Sepedi, with a preference for Xitsonga for small growers.
key statement: Should the grower pages also be in Xitsonga (and perhaps Afrikaans)? English is the minimum, and statements must be in English for the auditors; the consultant will price the translation.

proposed statement: Growers need to receive a printed slip for each truck leaving the weighbridge to avoid phone calls about fruit delivery.
key statement: Intake prints a small slip for each grower on the truck for the driver to take away; the carbon books stay as a fallback if the tablet fails, with a quick way to enter those tickets afterwards.

proposed statement: The weighbridge tablet may break during busy periods, so the system must have a backup method using carbon books.
key statement: Intake prints a small slip for each grower on the truck for the driver to take away; the carbon books stay as a fallback if the tablet fails, with a quick way to enter those tickets afterwards.

proposed statement: The client needs to split one truck's weight across several growers by their number of bins
key statement: One truck can carry several growers' bins (a contractor collects from six or seven small growers); intake splits the truck's net weight across growers by number of bins, and each grower's ticket shows his share. The contractor, paid by the growers directly, needs nothing from the system.

proposed statement: The system must have a single button for the tipper operators to scan bins
key statement: At the weighbridge, a rugged tablet rather than the PC, with big buttons usable with gloves and a screen readable in the sun; at the tipper, as close to one button as possible.

proposed statement: The system must have a single button for the tipper operators to scan bins
key statement: Packhouse users: two weighbridge clerks (one per shift, both together in the peak) and three tipper staff over the shifts, plus Precious and the foreman; the clerks are comfortable with WhatsApp and the WeighMate screen, the tipper staff less so.

proposed statement: The current process requires the manager to walk to the weighbridge to check daily bin counts and packout per cultivar
key statement: A daily summary for management of the previous day's bins received and packout per cultivar, emailed at 06:00 and on a page Johan can look at, also when he is away.

proposed statement: The client currently uses a spreadsheet for manual monthly reporting of volumes, packout, and advances paid
key statement: The board's monthly report (volumes, packout, advances paid), which takes Sipho a day by hand, stays in his spreadsheet in phase one, with the volumes and packout coming from the system.

proposed statement: The system must allow for per grower, per cultivar, per class, monthly totals in the export to spreadsheet
key statement: A monthly export for Sipho's spreadsheet with totals per grower, per cultivar and per class, with the delivery numbers alongside, not one row per bin.

proposed statement: The weighbridge intake must be live by the first of March
key statement: Weighbridge intake live by 1 March 2027 (first mandarins at the end of March); grower pages by the end of April 2027.

proposed statement: The grower pages must be live by the end of April
key statement: Weighbridge intake live by 1 March 2027 (first mandarins at the end of March); grower pages by the end of April 2027.

proposed statement: The system must be trained in February for weighbridge clerks and tipper guys
key statement: Training in February with practice days on made-up deliveries: two sessions for the packhouse team (shifts) and one for the office; a short manual with pictures; the consultant on site for the first two mornings of the season.

proposed statement: The system must include grower list with orchard blocks and cultivars
key statement: The grower list with its orchard blocks and cultivars (about 600 blocks, partly out of date, checked by Marietjie) is brought over from the spreadsheet; last season's deliveries only if cheap, to be decided once the consultant has seen the spreadsheet.

proposed statement: The system must have last season's deliveries data for comparison
key statement: The grower list with its orchard blocks and cultivars (about 600 blocks, partly out of date, checked by Marietjie) is brought over from the spreadsheet; last season's deliveries only if cheap, to be decided once the consultant has seen the spreadsheet.

proposed statement: The client needs to know how many queries each grower sends when they disagree with a packout
key statement: A grower can raise a query on a delivery from their page, which reaches Precious with the delivery, scans and grader report; phoning stays possible, and she sees how many queries each grower sends.

proposed statement: The packout should be visible to the grower immediately after grading, without waiting for Precious to check it
key statement: Does the grower see the packout straight from the grader, or only after Precious has checked the report (which would make her a bottleneck at about 60 batches a day in the peak)?

proposed statement: The packout should be visible on the grower's page on Saturdays
key statement: In the season the grower pages must be up on working days including Saturdays (the packhouse works Saturday mornings in the peak, when growers have time to look); an hour down is acceptable, a day is not. The consultant proposed 06:00 to 18:00, Monday to Saturday, with maintenance at night or out of season.

proposed statement: The packout should be visible to the grower immediately after grading, but the client will check it later

proposed statement: The system should have a backup power supply for the Wi-Fi access points to prevent network drops during load-shedding
key statement: Ruan will put a small UPS (about R3,000) on the packhouse Wi-Fi access points; Johan approved it.

proposed statement: The system should generate a weekly report for the export agent with carton counts per cultivar and class, ready by nine o'clock on Monday
key statement: A monthly export for Sipho's spreadsheet with totals per grower, per cultivar and per class, with the delivery numbers alongside, not one row per bin.

proposed statement: The client needs to collect crop estimates for each cultivar before the season starts
key statement: Growers can propose changes to their orchard blocks (cultivar, planting year, hectares) on their page, and the office approves them, because the spray records follow the block; today the co-op finds out only when the wrong cultivar arrives.

proposed statement: The client needs to collect crop estimates for each cultivar before the season starts
key statement: Collecting growers' February crop estimates (bins expected per cultivar, which the board wants before the season; now on paper forms that Marietjie chases) on their page: in phase one if there is time, otherwise next season, priced separately.

proposed statement: The client has a problem with growers not using the system, which could increase phone calls
key statement: If the small growers don't use the portal, the calls won't go down; mitigated by showing it at study group days and with the extension officer, Mister Baloyi, who visits every second week.

proposed statement: The client needs to update their membership forms to comply with POPIA regulations
key statement: The 2005 membership forms say nothing about POPIA; update them or send members a notice about the portal and SMSes before the season, with the wording checked by the lawyer member. Johan is the registered information officer.

proposed statement: The client has lost about a hundred bins annually due to poor tracking
key statement: Tracking the co-op's own bins, about 100 of which are lost each year.

proposed statement: The client prefers to see what growers will see before building the system
key statement: See the main grower screens designed first and reviewed with some growers before anything is built, and a half-hour progress update every two weeks showing working software, not slides.
